capabilities: Uploads attachments to S3-compatible, WebDAV or own-server storage
Embeds stored files in notes via keyhole:// links
Encrypts uploads end-to-end on the device
Moves existing attachments to storage and back again
Caches viewed files offline on the device
extras: Beta: tested on macOS and iPhone only, Android untested. Without Keyhole installed, embeds show as broken images, and Obsidian Publish cannot show Keyhole files. No telemetry; secrets live in the device keychain, never in the vault.
problem: Obsidian keeps attachments inside the vault, so vaults grow large and files stay tied to local disk, with no built-in way to keep them on your own private storage.

relations.evidence: keyhole-server: a small server of its own, no dependencies, Docker image

requires.name: S3-compatible storage (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, MinIO), WebDAV (Nextcloud, Synology) or a keyhole-server instance

summary: Plugin that stores attachments on your own S3, WebDAV or server storage and embeds them in notes via keyhole:// links, with optional end-to-end encryption.
